http2_concurrent_cancel.unchanged_test_source:
def test_eight_concurrent_connections_and_client_drop_release_targets(self):
        peer = self.fixture.peer("h2", tls=True, legacy=True)
        origin = self.fixture.origin(echo=True)
        size = 256 * 1024
        requests = [self.fixture.request(peer, origin, mode="cancel", size=size) for _ in range(8)]
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            reports = list(pool.map(lambda request: self.success(request, size=size), requests))
        self.assertEqual(len(reports), 8)
        self.assertEqual(len(origin.requests), 8)
        self.assertEqual(origin.received, size * 8)
        self.fixture.assert_accepted(peer, origin)
        self.wait_for(lambda: not origin.active)

readv_log_interpretation.explanation: The old CopyRawConnIfExist constructs buf.NewReader and on Windows always calls a function named readV. That function unconditionally prints CopyRawConn readv, even when NewReader selected SingleReader. With xray.buf.readv=disable the init switch leaves useReadv false and the reader factory selects SingleReader. The log text is not a report of the selected reader implementation.
readv_log_interpretation.conclusion: The same official legacy binary passed the unchanged eight-connection/two-second-release test in this run under the documented official environment override. This comparison does not establish a unique cause for the earlier failure.

limitations: Synthetic loopback peers only; no public-node test.
One successful Windows attempt does not eliminate the separately observed intermittent WSS outer-close error on Linux.
